newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fraud charges fly as French poll campaign opens.
newsitem.headline: Fraud charges fly as French poll campaign opens.

text.p: France's opposition threw charges of corruption and poll fraud at the conservative government on Wednesday as campaigning for next month's election got off to an ugly start.

Socialists and rightists accused President Jacques Chirac of calling the May 25-June 1 snap election for fear that fresh corruption scandals involving members of the government and the ruling coalition could be exposed.

"I am convinced, and I say it gravely and solemnly, that sleaze scandals were the major reason for dissolving parliament," Philippe de Villiers, leader of the rightist Movement for France, told a news conference.

Undaunted by indignant denials, Socialist party spokesman Francois Hollande raised allegations made on Tuesday by the satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine that Prime Minister Alain Juppe had told key allies he planned an amnesty on political sleaze if he retained power.

Juppe's office has dismissed the allegations as electoral slander, and Justice Minister Jacques Toubon said they were a fabrication. Ex-defence minister Francois Leotard, whose name was mentioned by Le Canard, called them nonsense and challenged the paper to say when and where Juppe could have told him this.

Scandals of illicit funding through rake-offs on public contracts have hit most French political parties for years, and an amnesty voted in 1990 by a parliament dominated by the left sparked furious charges of self-acquittal.

Media reports denied by both men have said Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot could soon be placed under investigation over the finances of the centrist CDS party.

Investigating magistrates are also probing Chirac's RPR party on suspicion that it systematically extorted kickbacks on public works contracts in the Paris region while the president was mayor from 1977 to 1995.

"The threats hanging over very highly-placed RPR figures are known...The government has probably tried to shake the scene to slow down the probes and get a free hand to push through an amnesty law," Hollande said.
Far-rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen has said Chirac called an early election because he feared the probes may get up to him.

The latest allegation to surface in the campaign, also made by Le Canard, was that the Paris city hall had over three decades padded with supporters the electoral roll of the capital's Left Bank fifth district, the constituency of Paris mayor Jean Tiberi.

Tiberi's Socialist opponent Lyne Cohen-Solal said she was taking court action over the charge that up to 4,000 voters -- nearly 10 percent of the district's roll -- were illegally registered there despite living elsewhere.
Le Canard said many of those voters had just failed to report that they moved out of the district, but many others were supporters who owed the city hall a favour.

Tiberi said non-resident voters were common in all the capital's districts. "Many voters want to keep voting in a district they love...I had no need of these votes to be elected," he told the newspaper Le Monde.
